title: Daily arXiv physics — Wednesday, 4 November 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; this is an inferred ordering, not a popularity ranking, and citation/independent-attention evidence is sparse for papers this new.

sections.title: SBi3PCF: cosmology with Dark Energy Survey Year 3 cosmic shear
sections.authors: David Gebauer, Anik Halder, Zhengyangguang Gong, Cora Uhlemann
sections.abstract: The authors apply simulation-based inference to DES Year 3 cosmic-shear two- and three-point statistics, detecting the integrated three-point signal and jointly constraining wCDM.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: First survey-data analysis of the integrated three-point cosmic-shear statistic with simulation-based inference; the authors report S/N 12.8 for the three-point signal, extensive pre-unblinding checks, and a 1.59× figure-of-merit gain over the two-point-only analysis.
sections.claimed_result: The DES Y3 joint fit gives Ωm = 0.272 (+0.038/−0.033), S8 = 0.784 (+0.024/−0.021), and w0 = −1.04 (+0.25/−0.19); the authors report at most 2.4σ difference from Planck 2018 plus BAO in the three-parameter comparison.
sections.evidence_type: observational; DES Year 3 weak-lensing shape catalogue analyzed with CosmoGridV1 N-body simulations and a learned likelihood
sections.unique_caveat: The result depends on the forward model and its treatment of intrinsic alignments, baryonic feedback, photometric redshifts, and shear calibration; the reported comparison with CMB+BAO is not a discovery claim.

sections.title: A New Precise Measurement of the e+e- -> pi+pi-(gamma) Cross Section with the Initial-State Radiation Method at BaBar
sections.abstract: The BaBar Collaboration measures the two-pion cross section from threshold to 1.4 GeV using 460 fb-1 of initial-state-radiation data and a pion-to-muon event ratio designed to cancel shared systematics.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A new full-dataset experimental measurement relevant to the hadronic-vacuum-polarization input to the muon magnetic anomaly; the ratio method reduces common uncertainties and the paper quantifies correlations with the 2009 BaBar result.
sections.claimed_result: For 0.3–1.4 GeV, the authors give the new two-pion leading-order HVP contribution as (525.9 ± 3.5_stat ± 3.8_syst) × 10^-10; combining their 2009 and 2026 measurements gives (517.8 ± 2.4_stat ± 3.3_syst) × 10^-10.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; 460 fb-1 of BaBar e+e- collision data using initial-state radiation
sections.unique_caveat: This is one experimental input over a specified energy interval, not by itself a resolution of the muon g-2 comparison; the HVP estimate inherits the cross-section measurement and its uncertainty treatment.

sections.title: Measuring the ultraviolet background at z≈3 from the quasar proximity effect in DESI DR1
sections.authors: Patrick Shaw, Rupert A. C. Croft
sections.abstract: Using 6,245 DESI DR1 quasars and mock-spectrum validation, the authors infer the hydrogen photoionization rate of the intergalactic ultraviolet background near redshift 3.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Large, named survey sample; the analysis calibrates its proximity-effect model on Astrid hydrodynamic mock spectra and reports statistical and systematic uncertainties separately.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain ΓHI = 1.376 (+0.095/−0.076 statistical) (+0.837/−0.521 systematic) × 10^-12 s^-1 at z≈3.
sections.evidence_type: observational; DESI DR1 quasar spectra, with Hubble-trained continuum reconstruction and Astrid simulation-based validation
sections.unique_caveat: The quoted systematic uncertainty is substantially larger than the statistical error; the result depends on modeling the quasar environment and its clustering bias.

sections.title: Fermi-LAT Detection of Extended GeV Emission toward the Middle-aged Supernova Remnant G156.2+05.7
sections.authors: Wei-Liang Xu, Qing-Wen Tang, Long Li
sections.abstract: An analysis of 17 years of Fermi-LAT observations finds extended GeV emission toward G156.2+05.7 and compares its spectrum and morphology with multiwavelength constraints.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Long-baseline Fermi-LAT data combined with radio, CO, and published X-ray constraints; the preprint says it is accepted for publication in MNRAS and reports a 3.4σ preference for spectral curvature.
sections.claimed_result: The authors detect an extended source with R68≈0.84°; their adopted multiwavelength model favors a hadronic contribution over a purely leptonic one, while also finding a proton-dominated alternative competitive.
sections.evidence_type: observational; 17 years of Fermi-LAT data plus radio and CO observations and published X-ray constraints, interpreted with spectral-energy-distribution models
sections.unique_caveat: The leptonic/hadronic partition is model-dependent; the Gaussian and uniform-disc morphologies are statistically indistinguishable, and the proton cutoff is fixed by assumption.

sections.title: UV spectra of little red dots: Broad-line N/C, gas recycling and black hole masses
sections.authors: Albert Sneppen, Darach Watson, Lucy R. Ivey, Kasper E. Heintz, Alex J. Cameron et al.
sections.abstract: JWST SPURS ultraviolet spectra reveal predicted broad emission and metal absorption features in several little red dots, which the authors interpret with radiative-transfer models of black holes embedded in dense gas.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct JWST spectral features test predictions of the Sirocco cocoon models; the paper combines emission-line ratios and absorption-line velocities to constrain abundance, density, and gas kinematics.
sections.claimed_result: For SPURS-GN-2 at z=7.19, the authors infer broad-line N/C = 12 (+3/−2) times solar and log ne = 9.7 (+0.3/−0.5); they interpret the absorption-line velocity ordering as stratified gas slowed by gravity.
sections.evidence_type: observational; deep JWST SPURS spectroscopy of four LRDs, interpreted with Sirocco radiative-transfer simulations
sections.unique_caveat: The sample is four objects, and the authors warn that strongly saturated absorption lines make direct abundance-ratio inference misleading; the physical interpretation is model-dependent.

sections.title: Quantum Error Correction in Nearly Critical Toric Codes
sections.abstract: The authors study decoding in a transverse-field toric code near its transition out of the topological phase and find finite thresholds for bit- and phase-flip decoherence using stabilizer measurements.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed between condensed matter and quantum physics; the work combines a proof about stabilizer measurements with numerically constructed optimal post-measurement decoders and reports thresholds arbitrarily close to criticality.
sections.claimed_result: For phase-flip decoherence, the authors prove the optimal post-measurement threshold is independent of transverse-field strength throughout the topological phase; near the critical point, they numerically demonstrate finite thresholds for both error types.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical and computational; transverse-field toric-code analysis, constrained lattice-gauge Monte Carlo, and numerical decoding
sections.unique_caveat: The claim that stabilizer measurements are an optimal decoding strategy is supported by theoretical evidence but not a rigorous proof; no hardware demonstration is reported.

sections.title: Beyond just a torus? Re-contextualising the AGN type paradigm using data-driven host galaxy quenching histories
sections.authors: Sahyadri D. Krishna, Vivienne Wild, Paul C. Hewett, Victoria A. Fawcett, Omar Almaini, Carolin Villforth
sections.abstract: A matched SDSS sample of about 3,000 Type-1 and Type-2 AGN hosts shows only a small fraction with recent rapid quenching, while Type-2 hosts generally have slightly younger stellar populations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted for publication in MNRAS; uses MFICA decomposition on a large, redshift- and luminosity-matched SDSS DR7 sample to test whether AGN type tracks host-galaxy star-formation history.
sections.claimed_result: The authors estimate that roughly 10% of the matched hosts rapidly quenched after a starburst within the last ≲1 Gyr; Type-2 hosts in that subset quenched at most 100 Myr more recently than Type-1 hosts.
sections.evidence_type: observational; SDSS DR7 optical spectra of approximately 3,000 matched AGN host galaxies, analyzed with mean-field independent component analysis
sections.unique_caveat: The authors give several possible explanations for the age difference, including torus covering factor, host obscuration, or AGN-type evolution; the matched observational result does not establish causality.

sections.title: SN 2019qem: decades of extreme mass loss before the explosion of a luminous, long-lived Type IIn supernova
sections.authors: Joysankar Majumdar, Mariusz Gromadzki, Takashi J. Moriya, David A. H. Buckley, Priscila J. Pessi et al.
sections.abstract: Multi-epoch optical and infrared observations of SN 2019qem, interpreted with circumstellar-interaction models, imply an intense mass ejection shortly before the supernova followed by a dense wind.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A data-rich, multi-epoch event study combining 26 optical spectra with optical and mid-infrared photometry; the authors submitted the manuscript to A&A and compare two interaction-model descriptions.
sections.claimed_result: In the preferred model, about 9 solar masses of circumstellar gas were ejected roughly two years before core collapse, with a subsequent wind near 0.6 solar masses per year for an assumed 100 km/s wind speed.
sections.evidence_type: observational; optical photometry and 26 optical spectra from −22 to +699 days, NEOWISE mid-infrared data, and thin-shell REDBACK circumstellar-interaction modeling
sections.unique_caveat: The mass-loss history and inferred progenitor mass depend on the interaction model and assumed wind/shock parameters; the authors note that light curves alone cannot separate circumstellar density from shock velocity.
